definitions.definition: The magnitude of the electrostatic force exerted by one point charge on another point charge is directly proportional to the product of the magnitudes of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
distractors: The magnitude of the electrostatic force exerted by one point charge on another point charge is directly proportional to the distance between them and inversely proportional to the product of their charges.
Each particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a gravitational force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses.
The electric field at a point is directly proportional to the distance from the charge and inversely proportional to the square of the charge.
The force between two charges is constant regardless of the distance between them, provided the medium remains the same.
The magnitude of the electrostatic force is directly proportional to the square of the distance between the charges.
The net charge of an isolated system is directly proportional to the product of the magnitudes of the charges.

definitions.definition: A region in space in which an electric charge experiences a force.
distractors: The electrostatic force experienced per unit positive charge placed at that point.
The rate at which electric charge flows past a point in a circuit.
The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to another.
A region in space where only magnetic materials experience a force.
The total amount of charge enclosed within a specific volume of space.
The force of attraction between two point charges.

definitions.definition: The electrostatic force experienced per unit positive charge placed at that point.
distractors: A region in space in which an electric charge experiences a force.
The electrostatic force experienced per unit negative charge placed at that point.
The work done to move a unit positive charge from infinity to that point.
The total charge divided by the distance from the point.
The force exerted on a test charge multiplied by its charge magnitude.
The potential difference between two points per unit charge.

distractors: Every charge in the universe is an integer multiple of the elementary charge.

Charges can be created or destroyed as long as the total number remains positive.
The total charge on a single object always remains constant.
The number of protons in an isolated system is always equal to the number of electrons.
The net charge of a system is conserved only if no friction is applied.

distractors: doubles.
becomes half ($1/2$) of the original force.
quadruples (4 times).
remains the same.

remains the same.
becomes eight times the original force.
becomes one eighth ($1/8$) of the original force.

proportionality.statement: The electric field strength at a point due to a point charge is...
proportionality.correct: inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the charge.
distractors: directly proportional to the square of the distance from the charge.
inversely proportional to the distance from the charge.
directly proportional to the distance from the charge.
independent of the distance from the charge.
inversely proportional to the magnitude of the point charge.
directly proportional to the square of the magnitude of the charge.

concepts.question: Which of the following is a correct rule for drawing electric field lines?
concepts.correct: Field lines must enter and leave surfaces perpendicular ($90^\circ$) to the surface.
distractors: Field lines originate on negative charges and terminate on positive charges.
Field lines may cross each other if the charges are of different magnitudes.
Field line density is uniform everywhere regardless of field strength.
Field lines form closed loops similar to magnetic field lines.
Field lines from a single isolated charge form concentric circles.
Field lines run parallel to the surface of a charged conductor.

concepts.question: What is the direction of the electric field vector at a specific point?
concepts.correct: In the direction of the force that a positive test charge would experience at that point.
distractors: In the direction of the force that a negative test charge would experience at that point.
Always towards the closest positive charge.
Always away from the closest negative charge.
Perpendicular to the direction of the electrostatic force.
In the direction opposite to the movement of electrons.
Parallel to the surface of the nearest charged object.

concepts.question: When substituting values into Coulomb's Law formula ($F = \frac{kq_1q_2}{r^2}$), how should the signs of the charges be handled?
concepts.correct: Substitute only the magnitudes ($|q|$) and use the signs strictly to determine the physical directions.
distractors: Always substitute the negative signs into the formula to calculate a negative force.
Ignore the signs completely, as electrostatic force is a scalar quantity.
Substitute the negative signs and take the absolute value of the final answer.
Only substitute the sign of the larger charge.
Substitute the negative signs and invert the calculated distance.
Add the signs of the charges together before substituting into the formula.
